records.description: CTU awards scholarships to foreign students under section 91(3)(b) of Act No. 111/1998 Sb. on Universities. The Master's track is a contribution towards the cost of a stay in the Czech Republic of up to CZK 10,000 per month for one to two semesters; the doctoral track covers the basic doctoral-study scholarship plus living costs of up to CZK 16,000 per month for six to twelve months. Both are financed equally from the rectorate's scholarship fund and the relevant faculty's fund, and neither covers tuition fees.

official.program_type: University scholarship for foreign students under Act No. 111/1998 Sb., section 91(3)(b)
eligibility: Master's track: a foreign student who wishes to take a Master study programme at CTU and displays qualities that entitle them to the award
Doctoral track: a foreign doctoral student capable of doing scientific work and studying on a doctoral programme in English language at CTU in Prague
Enrolled as a foreign student at the relevant faculty of CTU
Not eligible: Erasmus students at CTU
Not eligible: Erasmus Mundus students at CTU
Not eligible: Exchange students at CTU
Not eligible: CTU foreign students receiving a government scholarship
benefits: Master's track: contribution towards the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic up to CZK 10,000 per month
Doctoral track: the basic scholarship for doctoral study programmes plus living costs up to CZK 16,000 per month
Financed equally from the scholarship fund of the rectorate of CTU and the scholarship fund of the relevant faculty or part of the university
Master's track: extension possible on excellent study results up to the standard length of the Master study programme
Doctoral track: extension possible on excellent work outcomes up to the maximum standard length of the study programme
selection_criteria: Decisions on the award are made by the vice-rector on the basis of a recommendation by the commission of vice-deans for international relations
Master's track: excellent study results, evidenced by passing all prescribed accredited courses for the first year within the recommended time plan
Doctoral track: excellent work outcomes, evidenced by results published in an internationally reviewed journal or an application submitted for an international grant
Qualities that entitle the student to the award of the scholarship
application_process: Obtain the agreement of your faculty before applying
Apply through the International Office at your faculty to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate of CTU
Submit the application on the form published on the web pages of the CTU rectorate
Master's track extension requires passing all prescribed accredited courses for the first year of the Master programme within the recommended time plan
Doctoral track: the individual study plan under Article 30 point 1 of the study and examination regulations is binding and forms part of the application

Doctoral track: within three months of completing the study stay, the receiving workplace submits a brief final report with a copy of the publication or grant application to the Science and Research Department of the faculty
official.duration: Master's track: normally 1 to 2 semesters, extendable to the standard length of the Master study programme. Doctoral track: 6-12 months, extendable to the maximum standard length of the study programme.
key_dates: No application deadline or intake calendar is published on the CTU Scholarships page

verification.deadline_note: The CTU Scholarships page publishes no deadline and no intake calendar. It describes a standing procedure: obtain your faculty's agreement, then apply through the faculty International Office to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate.
verification.funding_period: per month (master's track; doctoral track up to CZK 16,000)
verification.tuition_coverage_note: The scholarship is a contribution towards the costs of a stay in the Czech Republic (Master's) or the basic doctoral scholarship plus living costs (doctoral). CTU does not describe it as covering tuition fees.
verification.english_requirement: Doctoral track: applicants must be studying on a doctoral programme in English language at CTU in Prague. No English test score is published for either track on this page.

the required language of the application documents

applicant_utility.description: CTU's scholarship is a living-cost contribution, not a fee waiver, so it will not make an expensive Prague year affordable on its own - it subsidises roughly a third to a half of a realistic monthly budget at the published ceiling. The application has to be brokered by your own faculty's International Office before it reaches the rectorate, which means the real first step is a conversation with your faculty coordinator rather than a form. Note that five categories of student are excluded outright, so anyone arriving through Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus, exchange, a government scholarship or another award should not plan around this.
eligibility_tips: The exclusion list is long and strict: Erasmus, Erasmus Mundus, exchange students, CTU foreign students on a government scholarship and any other scholarship holders are all ineligible. If you already hold another award, this one is closed to you.
The doctoral track requires an English-language doctoral programme at CTU Prague specifically - a Czech-taught or off-Prague programme does not qualify.
You must be enrolled as a foreign student at the relevant CTU faculty, so the scholarship assumes you are already inside the university system rather than applying alongside your admission.
application_tips: Start with your faculty, not the rectorate. The published route is: obtain your faculty's agreement, then submit through your faculty's International Office to the Department of International Relations at the rectorate.
Use the rectorate's own form. There are two distinct versions - one for Master study programmes and one for doctoral/MGR-PhD applicants - so download the correct one for your level.
For the doctoral track, prepare your individual study plan early because it is a binding part of the application under Article 30 point 1 of the regulations.
If you want an extension, the master's track requires every prescribed accredited first-year course to be passed within the recommended time plan; missing one lapses your entitlement to extend.
documents: The rectorate application form for your level, checked and confirmed by your faculty International Office.
Doctoral applicants: the individual study plan is not optional background - it is part of the application itself.
Doctoral applicants: keep evidence of the eventual publication or grant application, since the final report with that attachment is due within three months of finishing the stay.
mistakes_to_avoid: Applying without your faculty's agreement. The procedure makes the faculty's consent the first step, and applications arriving unbrokered will not follow the published route.
Assuming the maximum is automatic. Both tracks are worded as "up to" a monthly amount, so treat CZK 10,000 / 16,000 as a ceiling, not a promise.
For doctoral applicants, losing the entitlement by failing to produce a journal publication or grant application - the page names this as one of the required outcomes of the study stay.
Confusing this with tuition support. It is not a fee waiver and will not reduce your tuition bill.
applicant_utility.deadline_notes: There is no published deadline, which cuts both ways: you are not racing a calendar, but you also have no guarantee of when a decision will land. Build in slack for the faculty-to-rectorate routing, and if you need an extension, remember the master's track requires clean first-year course completion - falling behind on even one accredited course can end the extension entitlement.
